headline: Trustworthy computing, from hardware to AI agents.
intro: SEPT Lab designs trustworthy computing environments by tightly integrating hardware security mechanisms with software systems, so that private data and programs stay protected on platforms from personal devices to cloud AI systems.

thrusts.text: Uncover, understand, and defend against system and hardware vulnerabilities, across cloud systems, CPUs, GPUs, and AI systems.
Co-design software and hardware for secure and efficient AI systems.

themes.title: Verifiable AI
themes.summary: Evidence about what model ran, how it ran, and whether its results can be trusted, without revealing sensitive data.
themes.topic_line: zero-knowledge verification · LLM inference · model oversight
description: As AI systems enter high-stakes workflows, users need evidence that a result came from the claimed model and computation, ideally without revealing sensitive data. We study how such evidence can be produced for LLM inference and where proof-based (zero-knowledge) approaches fail. Hollow-LLM Attack identifies a security problem in zero-knowledge verification of LLM inference, while WAVE uses architecture-level observation to oversee model execution without exposing model data.

SEPT Lab also maintains [verifiable.pro](https://verifiable.pro/), a public resource on verifiable AI, starting with trusted execution environments. It offers news, explainers, and guides on what evidence can establish about an AI service's claims, and where the limits remain.

themes.title: TEEs and Confidential Computing
themes.summary: Make hardware-isolated execution practical: efficient, secure TEE-based systems for cloud and AI workloads.
themes.topic_line: SEV-SNP · SGX · confidential VMs and GPUs
description: Trusted execution environments (TEEs) such as AMD SEV-SNP and Intel SGX let cloud tenants run code and data in hardware-isolated contexts, and confidential VMs and GPUs extend this isolation to entire workloads. We build TEE-based systems and study what it takes for them to run efficiently, from oblivious memory access inside VM-based TEEs to communication in confidential multi-GPU machine learning. We also build defenses, such as automated detection of ciphertext side-channel vulnerabilities in cryptographic implementations.

themes.title: System and Hardware Vulnerabilities
themes.summary: Find the design flaws and side channels that break security guarantees, and disclose them to vendors.
description: We look for design flaws and side channels that break the security guarantees of systems and hardware, across cloud systems, CPUs, GPUs, and AI systems. Recent work examines RMP entry caching in AMD SEV-SNP, for which AMD published security bulletin [AMD-SB-3036](https://www.amd.com/en/resources/product-security/bulletin/amd-sb-3036.html); hidden risks in macOS application-sandboxed PID-domain services; electromagnetic side channels that reveal virtual reality app identity and activity; and attacks on AI models.

Earlier work on AMD SEV uncovered attacks through unprotected I/O operations, ciphertext side channels, TLB poisoning, and the power reporting interface; AMD confirmed several of these findings through security bulletins and CVEs.

themes.title: AI Agent Security
themes.summary: Observe and protect agent execution with TEEs and runtime monitoring.
themes.topic_line: runtime monitoring · tool isolation · agent memory
description: AI agents increasingly run on shared cloud infrastructure and handle sensitive data. We use TEEs and runtime monitoring to observe agent execution and to build trusted infrastructure for LLM systems and agents. Open problems include isolating tool execution and protecting long-lived memory and secrets.
open_problems: How to use TEEs or runtime monitoring to observe agent execution
How to protect long-lived memory and secrets
How to build trusted infrastructure for LLM systems and agents
How to defend against cloud- and hardware-level leakages in agent backends

projects.name: WAVE artifact
projects.description: Code for the ASPLOS 2026 paper WAVE. It observes GPU performance counters to check claims about model execution, such as a minimum model size, without exposing model data. Running it requires an NVIDIA GPU.

projects.name: ClawGang
projects.description: Infrastructure for valuable, tradable, and verifiable agent memory. ClawGang binds agent memory to verifiable computational provenance through TEE-based certification on AMD SEV-SNP. The repository includes the white paper.

projects.name: Muse MCP Adapter
projects.description: A user-controlled bridge between the Muse personal agent and MCP servers. The agent sees only the capabilities the user has reviewed, and every write is confirmed by the user first and runs at most once.
